headline: Visa Interview Halted Globally After Official Realizes They Are Just 'Reciting The Same Five Questions From A 1994 Brochure'
body:
"I was standing there in the embassy line for four hours, and suddenly the officer just stared at the wall, dropped his stapler, and whispered that he couldn't ask one more person about their 'intent to return' without losing his mind," said a software engineer headed for a conference.

"The official told me my file was fine, but he was taking a sabbatical to figure out if he actually existed as a person or just as a human-shaped vessel for high-frequency travel inquiries," reported an exchange student.

"I watched the consul shut the window mid-sentence and put up a sign that said 'The questions are fake, the answers are rehearsed, and the interview is a collective hallucination,' which is honestly the most honest service I've ever received," shared a travel blogger.

"My appointment was canceled because the entire staff reportedly gathered in the breakroom to discuss why we insist on asking people if they plan to 'overstay' when they have a return ticket clearly stapled to their chest," remarked a frustrated tourist.

"I tried to offer the interviewer a coffee to keep things moving, but he just stared at me and asked if my coffee had a 'non-immigrant' purpose, at which point I realized nobody was going anywhere today," noted a business consultant.
caption: Seems the embassy staff finally hit their limit with the monotony. ✈️🛑 #VisaPause #ExistentialCrisis #TravelDiaries #EmbassyLife (satire)
igHook: Would you keep working if you had to ask the same five questions every day for thirty years?
imagePrompt: A nondescript government office window with a flickering fluorescent light above and a long, blurred line of people waiting in a sterile waiting area.

sourceHeadline.title: Team Trump Pauses US Visa Interviews Worldwide. Here's Why

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 10 stands out by grounding the absurdity in a relatable existential frustration rather than a zany, non-sequitur premise. The tone is perfectly deadpan, the structure is clean, and it avoids the 'AI slop' trap of over-explaining the joke by letting the bureaucrat's quiet collapse speak for itself.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses a fictional, absurd scenario to satirize the bureaucratic nature of visa interviews. It avoids naming any real public figures, private individuals, or groups, and the image prompt is entirely generic.
